reason: Project lens: not refuted. The SEC at draw_column.cell (src/render.6502 ~1764) is in no PROTECT range or generated source. It is not raster-timed (the renderer in bank 4), and it touches no zero page or data. .cell is local to draw_column's braces and is reached only by fall-through: the other .cell at line 2116 is a different scope. The only outside references into draw_column are the symbolic self-modified operands (mask_operand, pix_operand and the _2 copies, from render.6502 1503-1526 and kindcache.6502), and these move with the code. C = 1 is guaranteed: col_ptr+1 comes from straight_sprite_hi,X, which is non-zero by the BNE known test, and the sprites are in ANDY &80xx-&8Fxx or bank 4 &9xxx-&B3xx. It is only ever INCed and cannot wrap, so LDA col_ptr+1 / ADC #&FF carries out whatever the carry in, and STA/TYA keep C. Paging and RAM read and written are unchanged. Room: 1 byte smaller, so it only eases ASSERT render_end/* <= REN_BASE. The 1-byte slide moves render.6502's tail, sprite_columns, sprite_straight (its pointer tables are LO()/HI() of labels), shield_hi and sky_edges. render.6502 has no ALIGN, and its alignment ASSERTs (the hist and column_buffer ones, rec_xh) concern workspace and buffers, not the code after line 1763. The dithered hills and MOUNTAINS data sit in bank4.6502 below &9000 and are unmoved. So the slide cannot change behaviour, only possibly add a page-cross cycle on an indexed table read, which the gate's speed check measures. No front-end, helicopter or game-over path differs, because the instruction is skipped only where C was already 1.
